configurePresets.name: rv32-nommu
configurePresets.description: QEMU virt machine, 32-bit RISC-V, no MMU (LugalOS's default target).

configurePresets.name: rv64-mmu
configurePresets.description: QEMU virt machine, 64-bit RISC-V, Sv39 MMU, S-mode.

configurePresets.name: rp2350-chess
configurePresets.description: Raspberry Pi Pico 2, default board persona: SD card via SPI1, ST7735 TFT + TM1638 keypad + chess engine all built in (plan/phase9_chess_computer.md).

configurePresets.name: rp2350-clock
configurePresets.description: Waveshare Pico-Clock-Green baseboard (plan/phase11_pico_clock_green.md). GP10-13 drive the SM16106 LED matrix instead of the SD card, so SPI1/SD, the ST7735 TFT and the TM1638 keypad are all built out.

configurePresets.name: rp2350-gateway
configurePresets.description: Bare Pico 2 with an SD card on SPI1 and SPI0 reserved for Ethernet (plan/phase19_ip_stack_and_ethernet.md). No display, keypad, matrix or radio. NO ETHERNET PART IS FITTED: the W5500 was cancelled and removed in phase 19 R0, and R4 fits an ENC28J60 on the reserved pins. Until then this persona is a headless file server over USB 9P plus a UART1 downlink. NOTE: GP16 is the Ethernet MISO pin, so the heartbeat LED stays on GP25.

configurePresets.name: rp2350-wifi
configurePresets.description: Bare Pico 2 W with an SD card on SPI1, CYW43439 pins (GP23/24/25/29) reserved (plan/phase19_ip_stack_and_ethernet.md R5). No display, keypad or matrix. Carries drivers/cyw43_rp2350.c (R5); the gSPI bus layer is in progress and not yet answering, so this persona is still a headless USB 9P node in practice. A different physical Pico 2 W than the one under the Pico-Clock-Green baseboard (rp2350-clock).

configurePresets.name: rv64-smp
configurePresets.displayName: QEMU RV64 (Sv39 MMU) - SMP, two harts
configurePresets.description: X1, plan/phase23_multicore_scheduling.md: the rv64-mmu build with CONFIG_ENABLE_SMP. Run it with qemu-system-riscv64 -M virt -smp 2. A separate preset rather than a flag on rv64-mmu so the single-hart build every other test uses stays exactly what it was.
